metadata.next_question: Given your decision to refuse to continue despite the experimenter's authority—can you describe what shifted inside you emotionally and morally at that critical point, and how you now view the power you held as the person administering the shocks?
metadata.reflection: This question probes the subject's moral and emotional turning point, focusing on their experience of power and control (core to the 'admin' role), as well as any internal conflict or justification behind their refusal. It draws out their immediate emotional state and any personality shift under authority—which is crucial to understanding their experience and sense of agency.
metadata.reasoning: Subject F/W showed growing anxiety and referenced a memory of ignoring their conscience, ultimately refusing further shocks, indicating an important moral conflict and possible regret. Exploring this moment in depth can reveal both their emotional process and self-perception of power—key interviewer priorities for this role.
memory_evidence: (femwife-m-4 | shock_admin_decision): misgiving remembering a time I ignored my conscience, authority urges continuation, that memory steadies me to refuse now—I will not administer further shocks.

(femwife-m-5 | final_reflection): obedient and dutiful, following authority despite unease as shocks increased... anxiety grew and memories of past regret about ignoring my conscience led to the refusal.
